sources_considered.why: Versioned primary documentation describes supported hosts and distinguishes requirements from recommendations.
Read to verify the March 31 release date of the documentation snapshot.
Contemporaneous results from the benchmark operator provide counterevidence to uniformly poor performance.
Later methodological disclosure limits confidence in the earlier benchmark results; used only as context.
The search result dates the benchmark run to April 10, outside the target period.

evidence_items.locator: FAQ passage discussing whether a Mac mini is needed
evidence_items.explanation: The documentation permits ordinary Linux hosts and describes a dedicated host as recommended rather than mandatory. This weakens a special-hardware reading, but a secured Linux host could satisfy Zitron's private-space alternative.

Strong scores on OpenClaw tasks challenge the broad poor-performance characterization. They are aggregate benchmark scores, not verified success rates for every task in Zitron's list or a matched comparison with ordinary chatbots.
The benchmark operator subsequently disclosed grading and scoring defects in version 1. This limits the weight of e2; it does not establish that the particular reported score was wrong.

unresolved_gaps: No representative comparison establishes total cost and complexity for equivalent completed tasks.
No sufficiently reliable target-period evaluation settles performance across the tasks named in context.
The benchmark article's publication metadata says March 18, 2026, but one leaderboard caption says March 18, 2025.
